candidateMeaning: Unselected numerical game-control hypotheses for later review, not empirical plant moisture values, new profiles or source assignments. A base profile and finite stock must first be explicitly approved; no candidate is installed or tested here.

limitations: No per-carrier wetness or ignition threshold/delay override exists.
Current profile overrides affect the whole trial by profile ID.
Reducing fuelAmount reduces combustible stock/energy, not a wet ignition barrier.
A finish adds an accounted combustible layer and is not moisture.
currentInterface.source: Coder Tinderbox source-only reply, 17 November 2026; existing shared carrier/profile interfaces

decisionsRequired: Approve or reject the proposed shared per-carrier data extension before code.
Select an existing base profile explicitly for each botanical family; no default is proposed.
Approve an actual finite dry-stock recipe/loading and local-share mapping independently of response.
Select or replace candidate static multipliers and dry-versus-sustained controls.
Keep all 412 current source parts withheld until those decisions and ordinary-tool evidence exist.

invariants: Default absence preserves existing nonplant behavior exactly.
No plant gets an implicit base profile, stock, zero or finish.
The existing profile's seconds and energy remain unchanged; no water energy is invented.
Finite dry combustible stock is measured/accounted separately from response.
Persist the explicitly chosen static response with the canonical owner through residency changes; never refill fuel.
No dynamic drying, latent-heat reservoir, evaporation, moisture transfer or weather integration is proposed.
futureContractRequired.purpose: An explicit static per-carrier material response applied to an approved existing base profile, rather than a new profile ID or global profile mutation.
futureContractRequired.scope: Future shared adapter/kernel contract only; it is absent from current tuples and fuels.

plannedControlsNotRun.hypothesis: Compare unchanged and chosen static response under the same finite ordinary-tool heat dose and native geometry, followed by cooling. Report char/ignition times and heat; do not assume a pass.
Choose a finite exposure reaching above both reviewed thresholds. Verify whether sustained exposure can ignite without hidden fuel or a drying solver; report failure honestly.
Same explicitly approved dry combustible stock in every response arm; stock/energy bookkeeping must stay finite and no visual reload refills it.
Nearby carriers using the same base profile retain their original parameters; a carrier modifier must not become a global profile override.
A damaged frond or canopy patch retires only its approved contribution and shares; visual followers and current stock agree.
Ordinary tools use the common inert-receiver path. No hidden ignition fuel appears on lagoon/basin water or other inert materials.
